meta.approval_rule_challenger: approve iff LR raw proba < 0.10 (LR is NOT calibrated; its 0.10 means something different from the champion's 0.10 -- labelled wherever used)
meta.note: All numbers computed from the data above; nothing invented. Rounded to 4 decimals except counts (integers) and money (integers, NT$).
meta.notes: | Gap fill Luna G1: m8_bootstrap_ci (B=2000, seed 42).

m8_validation_halves.note: Test 6.000 split stratified into halves A/B (n=3.000 each, seed 42). A validator re-checks outcomes on a fresh split: half-to-half swings show how much of a 'finding' is noise.

m8_tiering.note: Materiality for tiering (M8.2): the model decides over NT$ millions of credit limit on 6.000 test applicants; expected loss uses the CALIBRATED proba (0.7816 model), LGD 0.45, EAD = LIMIT_BAL. Scale to the full book by multiplying by (book size / 6.000) -- the test set is a 1/5 stratified sample of the 30.000-row data, NOT the live book.

m8_seed_sensitivity.note: Same split (seed 42), only the GBM random_state varies (42..46). Spread = max-min across 5 seeds; sd is ddof=1. A model whose ROC-AUC moves a lot when only the seed changes is not reproducible -- its '0.7823' is a lottery ticket, not a measurement.

challenger.model: LR (Pipeline StandardScaler + LogisticRegression, RAW proba -- not calibrated)

m8_champion_challenger.note: Challenger LR is evaluated on its RAW proba at the SAME 0.10 threshold -- its 0.10 is not the champion's 0.10 (LR is not calibrated; its Brier 0.1427 vs champion 0.1345). The profit gap is therefore partly a calibration artefact, not pure ranking skill -- say so in the lesson. McNemar tests whether the two models' DECISIONS differ more than chance, not whether one is better.

m8_shadow.note: Shadow mode: the challenger decides on the same applicants but its decisions are RECORDED, not acted on. The two cells above are what switching would have changed on this test set -- the price of the switch, measured before paying it.

m8_lr_calibrated_thr010.model: LR terkalibrasi Platt/sigmoid (CalibratedClassifierCV cv=3, estimator = Pipeline StandardScaler + LogisticRegression)
m8_lr_calibrated_thr010.note: M8.4 M3: calibrated LR at 0.10 approves FEWER than raw LR (1.166 vs 1.215) and earns only +NT$63.500 more (+1.886.500 vs +1.823.000) -- still NT$6.327.500 below the champion (+8.214.000). Calibration explains only a small part of the challenger gap; the rest is ranking (ROC 0.7427 vs 0.7816).

m8_approve_all_realised_loss.note: M8.4 S6: realised loss if EVERY test applicant is approved (sum LIMIT_BAL of default rows x LGD 0.45). This is NOT the expected loss 78.675.378 (sum of calibrated proba x LGD x LIMIT over all test rows).

m8_mean_scores_test.note: M8.4 S1: 0.2217 is the MEAN CALIBRATED PROBA on test, not the base rate (0.2212). Mean predicted proba != base rate; cite as 'mean calibrated proba [notebook]' wherever used.

m8_bootstrap_ci.method: Percentile bootstrap, B=2000, seed 42, resampling TEST rows with the calibrated GBM model FIXED (no refit). CI measures sampling uncertainty of the test set -- what a validator needs before calling a 0,06 pp breach 'real'.

bad_rate_pp.note: CI selisih bad rate antar-half MELEWATI 0 -- selisih 1,06 pp TIDAK signifikan pada 95%: sebagian besar CI di atas 0 tapi batas bawahnya di bawah 0.

age_60plus_n76.note: ECE AGE 60+ 0,1208 -- CI bootstrap SANGAT lebar: bukti kenapa n<200 adalah TEMUAN-INVESTIGASI, bukan pemicu band.
